question: Why is there no need to mention recitation and other practices once accomplishments come spontaneously?
premises: They appear in front of the practitioner.
Recitation and similar practices become unnecessary to mention.
inference: Since accomplishments arrive spontaneously, there is no need to speak of recitation and other practices.
plain_english: They come by themselves and stand before him—so what need is there to speak of recitation and the rest?
